title: Lena and the Will
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Halloway is exhumed for a centennial ceremony and found empty, coroner Orsen Delacroix is forced to reopen the case of his own mother's drowning twenty years ago — a death ruled accidental by the same men who now control Halloway's estate. Following a trail of forged signatures on the will, Orsen discovers the founder never died in Halloway's Hollow at all; he vanished to escape his heirs, leaving a second will naming Orsen's mother as executor. At the anniversary dinner, Orsen exposes the surviving conspirator — the town's revered matriarch, Vivian Halloway — who confesses before the assembled town, trading her freedom for the truth her father demanded: that loyalty built the town, but only truth could inherit it.
about_author: Beatrix Galloway is the pen name of a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing probate records and cemetery ledgers in rural New England. Her fiction is known for quiet, procedural mysteries where the dead are treated with more respect than the living.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Orsen Delacroix's POV. A routine autopsy closes the third 'accident' Orsen has quietly proven was murder, all buried in paperwork no one reads. Establishes their meticulous grief for their mother's unsolved drowning. Emotional beat: competence as armor, loneliness beneath it.

chapters.title: The Centennial Order
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The town council orders Edmund Halloway's remains exhumed for reinterment in a marble tomb ahead of the anniversary dinner. Orsen objects — the original burial records don't match the death certificate. Beat: first crack in the town's polished story.

chapters.title: Empty Oak
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV at the exhumation. The coffin holds only river stones wrapped in a funeral shroud. The crowd gasps; Councilwoman Vivian Halloway watches Orsen too closely. Beat: shock curdling into suspicion — someone here has known for forty years.

chapters.title: What the Police Called Closed
chapters.summary: Deputy Mara Quist's POV. Mara, who owes Orsen for saving her career, warns them off: the empty grave case belongs to county detectives. She slips them the old file anyway. Beat: loyalty offered, truth deferred.

chapters.title: The Drowned Woman's File
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In the archive, Orsen finds their mother's drowning report signed by the same coroner who certified Halloway's death — a man who died conveniently soon after. Beat: private grief fuses with public mystery; the cases braid together.

chapters.title: Vivian's Tea
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Vivian Halloway invites Orsen to the family house, charming and menacing, urging them to let the founder rest. She mentions Orsen's mother unprompted. Beat: dread dressed as hospitality; Orsen leaves certain she knows something.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara quietly pulls payroll and land records: three 'accident' victims all notarized documents for Halloway Timber in their final weeks. Beat: rising tension — the pattern isn't coincidence, it's cleanup.

chapters.title: The Second Signature
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Forensic comparison shows the 1985 will bears two different hands signing Edmund Halloway's name. Someone forged the founder's final wishes. Beat: cold fury; the inheritance everyone reveres is counterfeit.

chapters.title: Anniversary Approaches
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs via dinner invitations and gossip. The town prepares its celebration while Orsen requests the original will from the state archive — and receives word it was checked out last week. By whom? Beat: the clock starts ticking toward the dinner.

chapters.title: Night at the Records Hall
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Breaking into the county annex, Orsen finds the will returned — pages razored out — and evidence someone else searched it recently: a hairpin Vivian's style. Beat: trespass and revelation; the enemy is inside the family legend itself.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. County detectives order Mara to suspend Orsen's access. Torn between duty and debt, she copies the missing pages' index before complying. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal in one character's decision.

chapters.title: The River Remembers
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Reconstructing their mother's drowning, Orsen realizes she died the week she was named executor of a document no one can find — and near the old Halloway mill. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose; the personal case becomes the key.

chapters.title: A Witness in the Pews
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. At the founder's memorial service, an elderly groundskeeper, Silas, presses a rusted tin into Orsen's hand: inside, a photograph of Edmund alive in 1991, years after his 'death.' Beat: hope and terror — the founder may have chosen to vanish.

chapters.title: Silas Talks
chapters.summary: Silas's POV chapter. He drove Edmund to the train station the night he fled his children's greed, carrying a true will addressed to 'the coroner's daughter.' Silas has kept silent forty years out of love for the town. Beat: confession as burden lifted, danger ignited.

chapters.title: The Mill at Low Water
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Searching the drained millrace, Orsen recovers a lead-lined box: the true will, naming Orsen's mother executor, plus Edmund's letter predicting 'one of my blood will do what I could not.' Beat: triumph shadowed by threat — someone follows them from the mill.

chapters.title: Threats and Tea Again
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen's home is searched; the photograph is stolen. Vivian offers Orsen money, then a veiled threat about finishing what happened to their mother. Beat: fear meets defiance; Orsen refuses both gifts.

chapters.title: Mara Breaks Ranks
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara arrests the county detective who stole the photo — he's been on Halloway Timber's payroll for decades. Her badge is nearly taken; she chooses Orsen over the institution. Beat: loyalty realigned with truth; alliance sealed.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Before three hundred townspeople, Orsen stands during the toast and reads Edmund's letter aloud, laying the forged will, the three murders, and their mother's drowning before the town. Beat: climax — the glass raised freezes midair.

chapters.title: Vivian's Confession
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Cornered by the letter and Mara's evidence, Vivian admits her brother killed the witnesses and drowned Orsen's mother; she forged the will to protect the family name. She surrenders the ledger. Beat: villainy humanized — shame wearing pride for forty years.

chapters.title: Arrests at Dawn
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Warrants land before sunrise: Vivian, the detective, and posthumous charges against the dead brother. The town wakes to headlines that unmake its founding myth. Beat: justice administered without triumph; cost tallied honestly.

chapters.title: Reburial
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Edmund's true remains — located through his letter to a coastal parish — are laid to rest beside the honest stone. Orsen finally visits their mother's grave and reads her name aloud as executor. Beat: mourning completed; inheritance reclaimed as memory, not money.

chapters.title: The Glass Raised
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, months later. At a modest memorial dinner, the town raises a glass to truth instead of legend. Mara stays on the force; Orsen takes the elected coroner's seat. Final beat: loyalty and truth reconciled — the town chooses to remember rightly.
